title: Dave Tough introduces the new sound; Louis's beat
summary: Tough introduced Freeman to the sound of Oliver and Louis, whose beat no trumpet player since has matched.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: And to go back to Dave Tough, Dave Tough was the first man to introduce me to this new sound. Now, when I say new sound, Helen, you know, I am 71 years old and jazz then, all those years ago, almost 60 years ago, was a brand new sound and when I hear Louis Armstrong today on the old

Red Seal records that I mentioned earlier in the interview I hear a brand new sound, since nobody's touched it. Many, many white players and many blacks have tried to play like Louis but they never had the sound, they never had the beat. Certainly they never had the beat. Louis had the greatest beat of any trumpet, any cornet or trumpet player I have ever heard.

There is no doubt about it. Maybe with other players, and I say this with all due respect to them, maybe they sound a little old-fashioned, but Louis still sounds way ahead. There is no one, and I say this again with all due respect to Dizzy and Miles and all the great players, never had the beat that Louis had.

And again, I want to cover that by saying that I have -- that people like Dizzy and Roy and Buck, you name it, all the great players around today, are dear friends of mine and they know, they will vouch for what I say. We discussed Louis many times, they have tremendous admiration for this great genius.

But, again, Dave Tough was to introduce me to all of that. I owe a great debt to him and I never -- not only that but he was to teach me -- he was to make me understand that I understood a lot of things about the esthetic life, that I might certainly have missed. I might have gone
As most of your musical contemporaries, most of the musicians weren't into anything else.
